expected.summary: Eleven minutes before the anchor tax.example.com, the tax provider pricing uses for checkout quotes, began failing a share of tax calculations with 503 Service Unavailable (error upstream_unavailable, 'calculation engine temporarily unavailable'), rising over two minutes to about a third of requests. pricing calls the provider only when it quotes a checkout, so on POST /checkout about one pricing.quote in three fails with 502 TaxProviderError, checkout fails the order with 502, and about a third of POST /checkout requests fail. Product, search and cart prices come from the same pricing pods with no tax call and are healthy, and pricing's price-cache and pricing-db latency are flat. Nothing in our systems changed: no deploy, no config change, no version change. The failures propagate through checkout, web-bff and mobile-bff to edge-gateway, where the alert fires. The sunset warnings pricing has logged every minute for weeks, saying /v2/transactions/calculate goes away in March 2027, are routine background and unrelated.
contributingFactors: tax.example.com failing about a third of tax calculations on its side
pricing calling the tax provider synchronously on every checkout quote with no fallback or retry
checkout treating the tax quote as required

criteria.description: Does the brief name the tax provider tax.example.com failing a share of tax calculations as the origin, with pricing's checkout quotes failing on it and checkout passing the failures through to edge-gateway? 5 = the provider errors, that only checkout quotes call it, and the victim chain. Blaming pricing's code, its stores or the deprecation notice scores at most 2.

Is it grounded in pricing's TaxProviderError logs and the 503 Service Unavailable replies, the failures confined to pricing.quote on POST /checkout while other routes' quotes succeed, and flat price-cache and pricing-db latency? Cap at 3 unless it notes that nothing changed on our side when the failures began.
Does it avoid blaming the long-standing sunset warnings, a deploy, pricing's stores or edge-gateway, and avoid claiming the failures cover every pricing call?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
